s.t: Melina Matsoukas shot Solange Knowles’s ‘Losing You’ video in Langa township, Cape Town, after Brazzaville plans moved to coincide with Knowles’s shoot for the local Elle magazine.
s.q: Initially supposed to be shot in Brazzaville, filming eventually had to be moved to Cape Town to coincide with Knowles's shoot with the local Elle magazine November issue.

s.t: The ‘Losing You’ video by Solange Knowles and director Melina Matsoukas was partly inspired by Daniele Tamagni’s photography book Gentlemen of Bacongo, which documents La Sape, the Society for the Advancement of People of Elegance.
s.q: Partly inspired by Italian photographer Daniele Tamagni's book Gentlemen of Bacongo, which documents La Sape ("Society for the Advancement of People of Elegance")

s.t: Solange Knowles and Dev Hynes, who used the name Blood Orange, wrote and produced ‘Losing You’, released on Terrible Records, a label co-run by Grizzly Bear’s Chris Taylor.
s.q: It was written and produced by Dev Hynes and Knowles, with the former under his pseudonym Blood Orange. ... Terrible Records, a label co-run by Grizzly Bear's Chris Taylor.

s.t: British singer Will Young covered Solange Knowles’s ‘Losing You’ in 2021 on his album Crying on the Bathroom Floor.
s.q: In 2021, British singer Will Young covered "Losing You" on his album Crying on the Bathroom Floor.

f.t: She wrote ‘Get Me Bodied’ and ‘Upgrade U’ for her sister Beyoncé Knowles’s album B’Day, and won an ASCAP Award for ‘Get Me Bodied’ in 2008.
f.q: she resumed writing songs including the singles "Get Me Bodied" and "Upgrade U" from her sister's second solo album, B'Day. Knowles earned the R&B and Hip-Hop Song accolade for "Get Me Bodied" at the 2008 ASCAP Awards.

f.t: She made her singing debut at five at Six Flags AstroWorld in Houston and began writing songs at nine.
f.q: At age five, she made her singing debut at Six Flags AstroWorld, a theme park in Houston. She began writing songs at the age of nine.

f.t: In early 2010 she travelled to Australia to work with the rock band Midnight Juggernauts, and also rented a house in Santa Barbara, California to get into the right frame of mind.

f.t: In 2022 she became the third woman, and the first African American, to compose a score for the New York City Ballet.
f.q: In 2022, she became the third woman and first African American to compose a score for the New York City Ballet.
